complexity.notes: Timsort on an already-sorted input is a single ascending run, so sorted() is O(n) here; the constant number of index()/pop() calls are each O(n), keeping the total linear. However, the solution violates the problem's O(1)-space requirement via the sorted copy, and the index-recovery dance (including mutation via pop) is needlessly convoluted — two pointers directly on the input would give O(n) time and O(1) space with 1-indexed positions for free.
complexity.summary: Copies and re-sorts the array (redundant since the input is guaranteed sorted), then runs the classic two-pointer scan to find the pair of values summing to target, and finally recovers original indices with list.index(), handling the equal-values case by popping one occurrence and searching again.
